Plan a prediction-powered study in one call (agent-friendly interface)

ppi_design.Rd

A single entry point to the main design calculations, with inputs in planning terms. It is used by the MCP tools (pppower_mcp_tools()), by the agent skill in the agents/ folder of the source repository, and by the command-line script agents/skills/ppi-power-analysis/scripts/ppi_design.R, so all three give the same answers. Leave the sample size argument empty to solve for it, or give it to compute power.

Usage

ppi_design(
  design = c("mean", "two_sample", "two_proportion", "paired", "2x2", "inputs"),
  ...
)

Arguments

design

One of "mean" (one-sample mean or prevalence), "two_sample", "two_proportion", "paired", "2x2", or "inputs" (convert reported metrics into planning inputs).

...

Arguments for the chosen design:

"mean"

delta, N, and either r2 (with optional sigma_y2) or prevalence, sensitivity, specificity; optional n, power, alpha, and pilot_n with confidence to plan at the lower confidence bound for a pilot r2 (rho_lower_bound()).

"two_sample"

delta, N_per_group, r2_A, optional r2_B, sigma_y2_A, sigma_y2_B, n_per_group, power, alpha, pilot_n, confidence.

"two_proportion"

p_A, p_B, N_per_group, sensitivity, specificity, optional n_per_group, power, alpha.

"paired"

delta, N, sigma_d2, r2_d, optional n, power, alpha, pilot_n, confidence.

"2x2"

p_exposed, p_control, N, sensitivity, specificity, optional effect_measure ("OR" or "RR"), prev_exposed, n, power, alpha.

"inputs"

any of mse with sigma_y2; prevalence with sensitivity and specificity; pilot_r with pilot_n (and confidence).

Value

A named list with the labeled sample size or power, the classical comparison, the percent reduction in labels, and a notes vector of assumptions.

Examples

ppi_design("mean", delta = 0.2, N = 1000, r2 = 0.49)
#> $design
#> [1] "one-sample mean"
#> 
#> $outcome
#> [1] "continuous"
#> 
#> $target_power
#> [1] 0.8
#> 
#> $alpha
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> $labeled_n_required
#> [1] 110
#> 
#> $classical_n_required
#> [1] 197
#> 
#> $label_reduction_percent
#> [1] 44.2
#> 
#> $r2
#> [1] 0.49
#> 
#> $unlabeled_N
#> [1] 1000
#> 
#> $notes
#> [1] "Assumes the prediction model is trained before the study and that labeled units are chosen completely at random from the study units."                                                  
#> [2] "Uses the asymptotic Wald test with the optimal (oracle) tuning parameter. With an estimated tuning parameter, add about one label for Gaussian data, and more for rare binary outcomes."
#> [3] "Plan with a conservative (lower) R^2 if prediction quality is uncertain; overstating R^2 gives an underpowered study, while the test stays valid."                                      
#> 
ppi_design("mean", delta = 0.2, N = 1000, r2 = 0.49, pilot_n = 50)
#> $design
#> [1] "one-sample mean"
#> 
#> $outcome
#> [1] "continuous"
#> 
#> $target_power
#> [1] 0.8
#> 
#> $alpha
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> $labeled_n_required
#> [1] 136
#> 
#> $classical_n_required
#> [1] 197
#> 
#> $label_reduction_percent
#> [1] 31
#> 
#> $r2
#> [1] 0.3502
#> 
#> $unlabeled_N
#> [1] 1000
#> 
#> $notes
#> [1] "Assumes the prediction model is trained before the study and that labeled units are chosen completely at random from the study units."                                                  
#> [2] "Uses the asymptotic Wald test with the optimal (oracle) tuning parameter. With an estimated tuning parameter, add about one label for Gaussian data, and more for rare binary outcomes."
#> [3] "Plan with a conservative (lower) R^2 if prediction quality is uncertain; overstating R^2 gives an underpowered study, while the test stays valid."                                      
#> 
ppi_design("mean", delta = 0.05, N = 1000, prevalence = 0.3,
           sensitivity = 0.85, specificity = 0.85)
#> $design
#> [1] "one-sample mean"
#> 
#> $outcome
#> [1] "binary"
#> 
#> $target_power
#> [1] 0.8
#> 
#> $alpha
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> $labeled_n_required
#> [1] 458
#> 
#> $classical_n_required
#> [1] 660
#> 
#> $label_reduction_percent
#> [1] 30.6
#> 
#> $r2
#> [1] 0.4466
#> 
#> $unlabeled_N
#> [1] 1000
#> 
#> $notes
#> [1] "Assumes the prediction model is trained before the study and that labeled units are chosen completely at random from the study units."                                                  
#> [2] "Uses the asymptotic Wald test with the optimal (oracle) tuning parameter. With an estimated tuning parameter, add about one label for Gaussian data, and more for rare binary outcomes."
#> [3] "Plan with a conservative (lower) R^2 if prediction quality is uncertain; overstating R^2 gives an underpowered study, while the test stays valid."                                      
#> 
ppi_design("2x2", p_exposed = 0.4, p_control = 0.2, N = 1000,
           sensitivity = 0.8, specificity = 0.8, effect_measure = "RR")
#> $design
#> [1] "2x2 table, RR"
#> 
#> $target_power
#> [1] 0.8
#> 
#> $alpha
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> $labeled_n_required_total
#> [1] 135
#> 
#> $unlabeled_N
#> [1] 1000
#> 
#> $notes
#> [1] "Assumes the prediction model is trained before the study and that labeled units are chosen completely at random from the study units."                                                  
#> [2] "Uses the asymptotic Wald test with the optimal (oracle) tuning parameter. With an estimated tuning parameter, add about one label for Gaussian data, and more for rare binary outcomes."
#> [3] "Plan with a conservative (lower) R^2 if prediction quality is uncertain; overstating R^2 gives an underpowered study, while the test stays valid."                                      
#> 
ppi_design("inputs", pilot_r = 0.7, pilot_n = 60)
#> $r2_point
#> [1] 0.49
#> 
#> $r2_lower_bound
#> [1] 0.3633841
#> 
#> $confidence
#> [1] 0.9
#>

#> [1] "Plan with r2_lower_bound (one-sided Fisher z bound) to protect against an optimistic pilot."
